result.topic_en: Euler fixes the starting point of the integral ∫Z dx so that it vanishes at x = 0, and then describes the nearby varied curves αμ: they must be drawn continuously, but they may be either governed by an equation or freely drawn by hand, and are constructed by cutting each interval YV in an infinitely small ratio.

items.english: Let us see what idea we ought to form of those neighbouring curves αμ.

items.quote: has curuas continuo quodam tractu ductas effe debere, ita vt in iis nusquam anguli aliiue faltus deprehendantur; hoc folo notato, perinde eft fiue iftae curuae lege quapiam continuitatis vel aequatione quapiam contineantur, fiue fint adeo discontinuae, quafi libero manus motu ductae.
items.english: These curves must be drawn in a continuous stroke, so that no angles or other jumps are found in them; this alone being noted, it does not matter whether these curves are contained by some law of continuity or by some equation, or whether they are even discontinuous, as if drawn by a free motion of the hand.
